reading.body:
Enzu sells GPU procurement, colocation, and management, and claims its services can cut GPU infrastructure costs by up to 55%.

The company sits in the layer between AI builders and the physical capacity they need. Procurement, colocation, and management are the work of finding GPUs, putting them in a building, and keeping them running. That is the part of the stack where compute stops being an abstraction and becomes power, floor space, and hardware someone has to buy and operate.

The 55% figure is the company's own claim about its services, not a measured result. Nothing in the record shows how it is achieved, what baseline it is measured against, or which customers received it. The stated customer range, startups to enterprises, is likewise the company's own description.

The record is thin in a specific way. No products, lawsuits, or MCP servers are recorded, and the company's website is the only source of detail about its business. That means the offerings and the savings claim are unverified by any second source here. It also means there is no data on how much compute Enzu actually procures or colocates, where its facilities are, or what power they draw. Those are the numbers that would show whether a company at this layer is material to AI scaling, and they are absent.

profile_text.body:
Enzu is a for-profit company whose website describes it as a provider of GPU procurement, colocation, and management for AI infrastructure. It lists bare metal AI, GPU colocation, and fully managed infrastructure among its offerings, and says it serves customers ranging from startups to enterprises.

The company states that its services can cut GPU infrastructure costs by up to 55%. No products, lawsuits, or MCP servers are recorded for Enzu, and its site is the only source of detail about its business.
